text:
Bitcoin breached a critical 21-month low of $57,800 on July 1, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index collapsing to 11 — the deepest "Extreme Fear" reading of the year. June 2026 was the worst month on record for U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, with BlackRock's IBIT alone accounting for roughly 77% of the $4.5 billion in total net redemptions. Simultaneously, the EU's MiCA transitional period expired today, triggering an industry shakeout: only ~200 of 1,200+ previously registered CASPs hold full MiCA licenses, forcing unlicensed entities into emergency wind-downs.

The macro backdrop is providing no relief. The Federal Reserve holds rates at 3.50–3.75%, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.50% and the DXY at 101.35 — all reinforcing a high-opportunity-cost environment for risk assets. U.S. equities remain under pressure from persistent inflation and geopolitical tension in the Strait of Hormuz, keeping capital anchored in dollar-denominated havens and leaving digital assets without a near-term macro catalyst.
